title: hotfix: tighten SLO enforcer backoff & regional failover ordering to avoid thrashing under load
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Hotfix: fixes SLO enforcer thrashing by adding deterministic regional failover ordering, per-region cooldowns, and jittered backoff; reduces inadvertent load-shedding during transient spikes.
description:
Summary: Production incidents on 2026-02-18 and 2026-02-19 showed the SLO enforcer could thrash between backoff and regional failover decisions under high-concurrency bursts. The symptom was repeated rapid failover toggles and aggressive load-shedding that pushed downstream queues into overload. This PR implements a conservative, deterministic ordering and cooldown model to prevent oscillation and reduces the aggressiveness of immediate failovers.

Root cause: A race in the circuit-breaker manager allowed concurrent backoff resets and failover triggers. Two issues compounded: 1) regional failover selection did not enforce a consistent priority/order, so multiple regions could be queued for failover simultaneously; 2) the backoff algorithm used a shared timestamp without per-region cooldowns, which allowed rapid re-enablement and re-tripping in bursts.

What this change does: - Introduces per-region cooldown windows (configurable via config/regions.yaml) to ensure a minimum interval between failover actions for a given region. - Adds deterministic region ordering when evaluating failover candidates (regions are ordered by priority -> latency -> capacity). This avoids simultaneous competing failover actions. - Jitters backoff durations and moves to exponential+cap backoff to reduce synchronized retries. - Fixes race in pkg/circuitbreaker/cb_manager.go by adding an in-memory per-region state mutex and clearer state transitions. - Lowers the default immediate-load-shedding aggressiveness threshold and adds a smoothing window for short spikes. - Adds telemetry: new metrics slo_enforcer.failover_decision, slo_enforcer.region_cooldown_start, slo_enforcer.backoff_jitter_applied and tracing spans around decision points. - Controlled rollout behind feature flag sla.slo_enforcer.stability_mode (default=true for this hotfix) so we can revert quickly if regression seen.

Files changed at high level: services/slo-enforcer/enforcer.py (core logic and telemetry), pkg/circuitbreaker/cb_manager.go (race fix and mutex), config/regions.yaml (cooldown defaults), kubernetes/overrides/slo-enforcer-deployment.yaml (env flags and rollout), tests/slo_enforcer/test_backoff.py (new regression tests), services/slo-enforcer/README.md (operational notes).

Testing done: - Unit tests updated and passing (tests cover per-region cooldown and jitter behavior). - Integration test harness ran a synthetic burst scenario for 10k requests; observed zero failover oscillations compared to 4 toggles on main. - Staging rollout for 24h with canary at 10%: metric slo_enforcer.failover_toggles reduced by 96% vs baseline. - CI: unit-tests / integration-tests / lint / e2e all passing (see CI checks below).

Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main and promote hotfix image to staging. 2) Canary at 5% for 2h, monitor slo_enforcer.failover_toggles, regional load-shedding counts, and end-to-end latency. 3) Ramp to 25% for 6h, then 100% if stable. 4) If any regression, flip feature flag sla.slo_enforcer.stability_mode=false to revert.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added and passing - [x] Integration test case for burst/oscillation - [x] Telemetry and tracing added - [x] Feature flag gating - [x] Docs updated with operational playbook - [x] Reviewed and approved by SREs

References: Linear ENG-1298, incident SUP-312 (2026-02-18 incident postmortem).
